cards.explanation: The answer is glad, friends. Isaiah says, "The wilderness and the dry land will be glad…" (Isaiah 35:1). I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and glad was not the word I'd have picked.

The answer is True. Isaiah says "The glory of Lebanon will be given to it, the splendor of Carmel and Sharon." (Isaiah 35:2). Lebanon, Carmel and Sharon are all names for lush, beautiful places. The desert gets handed all of it. That's quite a gift for a patch of sand.
The answer is the LORD's glory, friends. Isaiah says, "They will see the glory of the LORD, the splendor of our God." (Isaiah 35:2). The blooming is wonderful, but all the eyes are on the LORD.

The message is to be strong and not fear. Isaiah says to tell those with anxious hearts, "Be strong, do not fear!" (Isaiah 35:4). Five words and a whole lot of comfort. Those are the words for anxious hearts.

The answer is False, friends. The anxious hearts are the ones being comforted. Isaiah says, "Behold, your God will come with vengeance. With divine retribution He will come to save you." (Isaiah 35:4). He comes to save them.

The answer is True, and it's right there in the verse. Isaiah says, "Then the eyes of the blind will be opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped." (Isaiah 35:5). Blind eyes and deaf ears sit side by side. Eyes and ears, both covered.
The lame will leap like a deer, friends. Isaiah says, "Then the lame will leap like a deer…" (Isaiah 35:6). I'd love to see that, though I'd need to get my base out of the way.

Grass and reeds and papyrus will grow there. Isaiah says, "In the haunt where jackals once lay, there will be grass and reeds and papyrus." (Isaiah 35:7). Papyrus is a tall plant that grows where there's water. A jackal's old hangout turns into a green, wet place.
The word is unclean, friends. Isaiah says, "The unclean will not travel it—only those who walk in the Way…" (Isaiah 35:8). The road has a clear rule about who's on it.

The answer is False, friends. Isaiah says, "And there will be a highway called the Way of Holiness. The unclean will not travel it—only those who walk in the Way—and fools will not stray onto it." (Isaiah 35:8). The fools part is right there at the end of the verse.

The answer is with singing, friends. Isaiah says, "So the redeemed of the LORD will return and enter Zion with singing, crowned with everlasting joy." (Isaiah 35:10). Crowned with everlasting joy is how the verse describes them as they come in.
